key_insight: The paper shows that real-space turbulent energy transfer at scale ℓ can be written directly in terms of local strain self-amplification and vortex stretching, with a geometric coefficient set by the spherical neighborhood’s moment of inertia.
engineering_relevance: This provides a mechanical, scale-local way to diagnose forward and inverse cascade events from flow kinematics, useful for turbulence modeling and analysis.
method: Exact geometric decomposition of energy transfer on a spherical fluid neighborhood
Separate the transfer into strain self-amplification and vortex-stretching terms
Further split transfer into longitudinal and transverse components to connect with Kolmogorov’s 4/5 law
evidence_signal: Direct numerical simulations confirm the decomposition captures the dominant local transfer and identifies a statistical boundary between forward- and inverse-cascade events.
watch_item: The result is derived for spherical neighborhoods and idealized DNS settings, so practical use in complex geometries or coarse experimental data may require care.
paper_title: Geometric Mechanics of Real-Space Energy Transfer in Turbulence
